-   **Rarity note:** Common species in Florida, found in sunny areas where milkweeds are present.

## Natural history notes

A large milkweed butterfly characterized by bright orange wings with black veins, broad black borders, and white spots along the wing edges, with males showing small black scent patches on the hindwings. In Florida, it is found in gardens, prairies, fields, roadsides, pine flatwoods, coastal areas, and other sunny habitats where milkweeds and nectar plants are available. Adults feed on nectar from many flowers, while the caterpillars feed exclusively on milkweeds and store defensive chemicals that make them distasteful to many predators.
